chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Rifa'ah ibn Musa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The woman is returned (from the marriage contract) due to al-'afal, al-baras, al-judham, and al-junun; as for what is other than that, she is not returned.

key_terms.الرّدّ: Return (of the wife/dowry due to defect)
key_terms.الْجُذَام: Leprosy (often distinguished from baras in medical jurisprudence)
key_terms.الْعَفَل: A specific type of eye defect or blindness

ai.seo_question: What are the specific physical and mental defects that allow for returning a wife in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing a definitive list of four major defects—leprosy, blindness, madness, and leprosy (or specific skin disease)—that warrant the right of return (rad) in marriage. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it limits the scope of 'defects' to these specific, severe conditions, thereby excluding other minor physical or mental ailments from invalidating the marriage contract. The exclusion of 'what is other than this' underscores the principle that marriage remains valid unless one of these specific, debilitating conditions is present.
